territorial_scope.description: Federal statute amending the United States Controlled Substances Act; applies to electronic communication service providers and remote computing services as defined, with no separate geographic provision in the operative text.

evidence.quote: the term `provider` means an electronic communication service provider or remote computing service;

summary.short: Proposed federal law adding Controlled Substances Act Sec. 521, requiring electronic communication service and remote computing service providers to report to the Attorney General facts indicating certain fentanyl, methamphetamine, counterfeit or unauthorized prescription drug crimes, within 60 days of actual knowledge.
summary.long: The bill would add Section 521 to the Controlled Substances Act. Providers of electronic communication services and remote computing services would have to submit reports to the Attorney General as soon as reasonably possible, and no later than 60 days after obtaining actual knowledge, of facts or circumstances establishing crimes involving fentanyl or methamphetamine, counterfeit substances, or unauthorized prescription pain medication or stimulants. Reports must include provider contact details and, to the extent reasonably available, account identifying information, but not the contents of wire or electronic communications except as provided. Providers may also report on a reasonable belief. The Attorney General must conduct a preliminary review, may investigate or close reports, must limit storage and delete reports after use, and must publish an annual report. Knowingly failing to report is unlawful and carries a fine of not more than $190,000 for an initial violation and $380,000 for subsequent violations. Knowingly submitting materially false reports carries a civil penalty of $50,000 to $100,000. Law enforcement officers may not submit reports, and broadband and text messaging providers are exempt. The bill also adds disclosure exceptions to the Stored Communications Act and states that no monitoring duty is created. The text states no separate effective date for these provisions.

relations.target_text: Stored Communications Act (18 U.S.C. 2702, title 18, United States Code)
relations.note: Amends subsections (b) and (c) of section 2702 to add disclosures to the Attorney General in connection with a report under new CSA Sec. 521; a further technical amendment to 2702(b)(7) is also made.

New CSA Sec. 521(i)(3) states that the section does not replace, amend or interfere with authorities and duties under 2703; Sec. 521(i)(1)(A)(ii) refers to requests to continue preservation under 2703(f).

notes: Relations cover only references stated in the introduced bill text (dated July 17, 2025). No legal_basis or enacted_by_bill relation is stated in the text. Target instruments have no registry IDs in this text, so target_instrument_id is left empty. The Controlled Substances Act is identified in the bill by its 21 U.S.C. 871 et seq. citation and, in the table-of-contents amendment, by its Public Law 91-513 name. Sec. 521(b)(1)(A) sets reporting 'as soon as reasonably possible' and also 'not later than 60 days' after actual knowledge; both are stated and coded as written. Several passages of the amended text have irregular indentation, so provision numbers follow the bill's own subsection labels.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes scope, eligibility, exemption or obligation tier was found. The numbers in the bill are penalty amounts in sec. 521(f) (coded as enforcement), reporting, preservation and notification periods in sec. 521(b)(1) and (i)(1) (coded as events), and the annual report deadline in sec. 521(j) (coded as an event).
